title: AI Daily Brief - 2026-06-02
tags:

---

## Today in One Minute

- JetBrains released Mellum2, a 12B mixture-of-experts coding model, while Towards Data Science published a workflow for pairing Claude Code with OpenAI Codex for stronger coding assistance.
- NVIDIA introduced Cosmos 3, an open "omni-model" for physical AI reasoning and action, alongside a Factory Operations blueprint and an expanded global AI cloud ecosystem.
- Google shared how it used Gemini to build the I/O 2026 site and a vibe-coded quiz in Google AI Studio, showing practical end-to-end use of AI tools.

## What Happened

- JetBrains launched Mellum2, a 12B-parameter mixture-of-experts model focused on code, available on Hugging Face. Separately, a Towards Data Science article walks through combining Claude Code and OpenAI Codex in one workflow so each tool covers the other's weaknesses.
- NVIDIA released Cosmos 3, described as the first open omni-model for "physical AI" - reasoning about and acting in the physical world (robots, factories, vehicles). NVIDIA also published a Factory Operations blueprint that wires AI into factory floors, and announced a wider AI cloud ecosystem with Taiwan-based hardware partners.
- Google posted two practical write-ups: one on how the I/O 2026 event website was built using Gemini, and another on a small interactive I/O quiz "vibe coded" in Google AI Studio, illustrating how non-specialists can prototype with natural-language coding.

## Why It Matters

- Coding-focused models and dual-assistant workflows are directly relevant to SoI/IT diplomas. Students should understand that no single AI coder is best at everything, and that comparing outputs is now a real engineering skill.
- Physical AI moves AI beyond chatbots and into engineering, robotics, and manufacturing-relevant diplomas (Engineering, SEG, ATS). Cosmos 3 being open means students can read about and discuss real model capabilities, not just marketing claims.
- "Vibe coding" with tools like Google AI Studio lowers the barrier for non-IT students and lecturers to build small interactive learning artefacts - quizzes, demos, simple apps - without deep programming background.

## Try This Today

- Open Hugging Face on your Windows 11 laptop and read the Mellum2 model card. Note its size, intended use, and limitations, then write a one-paragraph summary you could share with students about when a specialised coding model beats a general chatbot.
- Give the same small coding task (e.g. "write a Python function to clean a messy CSV of student marks") to two AI assistants you already have access to (e.g. Copilot in Edge and ChatGPT). Compare correctness, comments, and error handling - this mirrors the Claude Code + Codex pairing idea.
- Spend 10 minutes in Google AI Studio trying to "vibe code" a 3-question quiz on a topic from your module. Note where the AI guessed wrongly about your intent - that becomes a teaching example about prompt clarity.
- Skim the NVIDIA Cosmos 3 post and list two ways a "physical AI" model differs from a text-only LLM. Use this to prepare a 2-minute classroom explainer.

## Teaching Angle

- Run a short "two-assistant bake-off" lab: students solve a coding problem using two AI tools and submit a reflection on which was better and why. Reinforces critical evaluation rather than blind trust, anchored on the Claude Code + Codex article.
- Use the Google I/O 2026 build and quiz posts as a case study in AI-assisted product work. Ask students to identify which parts a human still had to design, decide, or correct - useful for media, UX, and IT diplomas.
- For engineering and applied science classes, use Cosmos 3 and the NVIDIA Factory Operations blueprint as a discussion prompt: where in a real factory would AI reasoning help, and where would it be risky? Tie this to safety, ethics, and human oversight.
- Set a quick reflection question for any class: "If a 12B model like Mellum2 can be downloaded and run by hobbyists, what does that mean for how we assess coding assignments?" Encourages honest conversation about AI use in assessments.

## Links

- [Introducing Mellum2: A 12B Mixture-of-Experts Model by JetBrains](https://huggingface.co/blog/JetBrains/mellum2-launch)
- [How to Combine Claude Code and Codex for Maximum Coding Power](https://towardsdatascience.com/how-to-combining-claude-code-and-codex-for-max-coding-power/)
- [Welcome NVIDIA Cosmos 3: The First Open Omni-model for Physical AI Reasoning and Action](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/cosmos-3-for-physical-ai)
- [NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint Gives Factories a New AI Brain](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/factory-operations-fox-blueprint-ai-brain/)
- [NVIDIA AI Cloud Ecosystem Expands Worldwide to Meet Global AI Compute Demand](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ai-cloud-ecosystem/)
- [How we used Gemini to build Google I/O 2026](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/io-2026-google-ai/)
- [Take our I/O 2026 quiz, vibe coded in Google AI Studio](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/io-2026-vibe-coded-quiz/)
